title: Autoscaler rollback safety net + nightshift heuristics
content:
Purpose:
Quick notes and working-runbook for building an autoscaler rollback safety net and pragmatic heuristics for nightshift oncall when a Dedicated GPU pool degrades. This is intentionally rough — the goal is something an oncall can follow at 2am without reading ten docs.

Background / Why this came up:
- Last week we saw a ~30% sustained latency regression in the eu-west pool during low QPS hours (02:10–03:30). Autoscaler attempted a downscale based on CPU signals; eviction + scheduling churn amplified the regression.
- Root cause: misaligned scale-to-zero/scale-in policy combined with a conservative eviction threshold on allocator; small drop in util caused aggressive downscale which then triggered cold-warm transitions for many hosts.
- Outcome: several in-flight requests timed out; fallbacks to smaller model variants increased cost and error surface.

Primary goals of this doc:
1) Provide immediate checklist for oncall to detect and (if needed) rollback autoscale decisions safely.
2) Establish nightshift heuristics to avoid aggressive automated scale-in during low-latency SLO windows (02:00–04:30 local).
3) Track short experiments to reduce false-positive scale-ins (hysteresis, min-running-capacity, synthetic-keepalive).

Signals to watch (metrics / dashboards) — quick reference:
- gpu_pool_utilization_pct (1m, 5m) — sharp drops that precede downscales
- allocator_eviction_rate_per_min — spikes after scale actions
- request_tail_latency_p95 / p99 — slowdowns after node removal
- alive_instances_count_by_pool — effective capacity
- pending_queue_depth and queue_time_ms — scheduling backpressure
- autoscaler_decision_log (events) — reason codes: target_cpu, target_util, safety_override
- cloud-instance-termination-events (provider logs) — to correlate scheduled terminations

Nightshift heuristics (fast rules for 2am–5am):
- If p95 latency > SLO and alive_instances_count fell in the last 15m, assume a scale-in cascade.
- Put autoscaler into "safety" mode: disable scale-in for 30 minutes (via toggle: /ops/featureflags/autoscaler-safety).
- If autoscaler was manually toggled off in last 24h, consult the owner before changing (check oncall notes).
- Minimum pool floor: enforce min_instances = max(ocup_current_instances, 0.5 * configured_pool_capacity) for night window as temporary guard.
- Keep a synthetic-keepalive job running (small no-op jobs every 5m) in night window to prevent cold starts for pinned hosts.

Immediate triage checklist (ordered, executable):
1) Confirm incident: open the "dedicated-pool-health" dashboard and note when alive_instances_count decreased and latency rose.
2) Look at autoscaler_decision_log for last 30m and copy the event ids.
3) If scale-in happened in last 10m and p95 > SLO, perform a rollback: set autoscaler policy -> "prevent-scale-in" for affected pool. Command: kubectl patch cm autoscaler-config -n redwood --type merge -p '{"data":{"prevent_scale_in_pools":"<pool-name>"}}' (Ops runbook entry).
4) If rollback toggle not available or kubectl patch fails, manual mitigation: raise min_instances for the pool in allocator-admin UI or via API: POST /allocator/v1/pools/<pool>/patch {"min_instances": <current + 2>}
5) Restart the synthetic-keepalive cronjob for the pool (namespace: dedicated-monitoring): kubectl rollout restart cronjob/keepalive-<pool> -n dedicated-monitoring
6) If evictions show high rates, temporarily set eviction_threshold to 0.85: kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: allocator-tuning
  namespace: redwood
data:
  eviction_threshold: "0.85"
EOF
7) If carrier-level terminations (cloud logs) coincide, open cloud console and check termination reason (preemptible vs scale action).

Post-rollback stabilization steps:
- Monitor p95/p99 and pending_queue_depth for 15 minutes. If latency normalizes, keep prevent-scale-in for 30–60m then gradually re-enable with higher hysteresis.
- Capture exact autoscaler event ids and add to incident ticket.
- Run a targeted synthetic hammer at 50% of normal QPS to validate that new floor prevents recurrences.

Hypotheses to validate (experiments list):
H1: Aggressive scale-in in low traffic windows causes cold-warm transitions that dominate latency regression. Test: increase scale-in-hysteresis window from 3m -> 12m for night window, measure p95 over 2 weeks.
H2: Short-lived bursts were misattributed to a reduction in customer traffic due to sampling error in target metric. Test: switch autoscaler input to a smoothed metric (EMA-60s) and compare alert rate.
H3: KV cache thrash is amplified when instances are removed; adding a delayed cache-eviction grace window reduces p99. Test: set cache-eviction-delay to 45s and observe.

Safe rollback policies (proposal):
- emergency-toggle: oncall can flip to disable scale-in for a pool; must include reason and ticket id. Toggle auto-expires in 60m unless extended.
- auto-detection guard: if p95 jumps > 40% within 15m of a scale-in, autoscaler enters passive mode and waits 20m before next scale action.
- min-instance soft floor: per-pool night window floor (configurable per region).

Runbook quick commands (copy-able):
- list recent autoscaler events: kubectl logs deploy/autoscaler -n redwood --since=30m | grep "Decision" | tail -n 50
- set prevent-scale-in flag (feature toggle): curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN' https://ops-api.internal/featureflags -d '{"flag":"autoscaler.prevent_scale_in","value":"true","pool":"eu-west-1-dedicated"}'
- bump pool min instances: curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN' https://allocator.internal/api/v1/pools/eu-west-1-dedicated/patch -d '{"min_instances":6}'
- restart keepalive: kubectl rollout restart cronjob/keepalive-eu-west-1-dedicated -n dedicated-monitoring

Communication template for oncall to post to incident channel:
- Short: "Investigating eu-west dedicated pool latency spike. Detected aggressive scale-in at 02:12; applied temporary prevent-scale-in and bumped min_instances. Monitoring p95/p99 and queues. Will update in 10m. (JIRA-CR-1882) — @oncall"

Open questions / TODOs:
- Who should own permanent night-floor config? product or platform? (need decision)
- Add a per-pool smoke test that runs right after any scale action to validate latency within 120s — engineering follow-up (owner: Miguel).
- Audit: tie autoscaler_decision_log entries to allocator incident ids automatically (follow-up PR).

Notes from last experiment (2025-08-28):
- Increased scale-in hysteresis to 8m for test pool; saw 12% reduction in post-scale p95 spikes but 6% higher steady-state cost. Tradeoff noted.
- Eviction threshold at 0.9 tolerated better than 0.85 in single-run test; but interacting with pod-scheduler we saw queue buildup for certain job shapes.

Appendix: quick checklist for handover to morning SRE (what to include in ticket)
- Exact timestamps of scale-in event(s) and rollback decision(s)
- Logs: autoscaler logs, allocator logs, cloud termination events
- Commands executed and feature toggles flipped
- Short summary of hypothesis and next experiment (owner + timeline)

If this doc is useful, I'll: 1) convert into a dedicated short-runbook in ops-runbooks/ and 2) draft a small automation to detect p95 spike within 15m of a scale-in and auto-apply safety toggle (requires product approval).

Raw scratch notes (2am scribbles):
- saw evict-rate spike at 02:14; p95 from 120ms -> 380ms; alive nodes -3 in 6m. toggled prevent-scale-in at 02:20. p95 down to 150ms in 12m. keepalive restarted. queue depth - stabilized.
- check cloud events: 02:13 termination reason = SCALE_DOWN_REQUEST from autoscaler v2.1.3
- next: add smoke-run after scale events

End of notes.
